purpose: Extended spoken-language normalization for vibe coding, programming, structured data, configuration, spreadsheets, developer tools, APIs, SQL, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, shell syntax, paths, Git, Docker, infrastructure, testing, data manipulation, CSS, Tailwind CSS, UI styling, Markdown, and technical instructions.

architecture.principle: Do not merely replace words with tokens. Recover what the speaker is attempting to communicate, preserve the intent, and emit canonical syntax when confidence is high.

function_call_syntax.spoken: call the function with no arguments
call it with user and id

cell_reference_patterns.spoken: range a one to a ten

api_url_patterns.spoken: api slash users question mark page equals one
api slash users question mark search equals john

spreadsheet_output_rules.rule: Treat spreadsheet references, formulas, ranges, columns, rows, percentages, currencies, and operators as technical syntax.

examples.spoken: sum a one through a ten
average b two through b twenty
if c two is greater than ten
count if d one through d one hundred equals active
multiply a one by b one
divide c two by d two

json.rule: JSON must use double-quoted keys and string values.

example.spoken: name colon John comma active colon true

yaml.rule: YAML uses key-value pairs, indentation, and list markers.

example.spoken: name colon John new line roles dash admin

toml.rule: TOML uses sections and equals signs.

example.spoken: server section port equals three thousand

csv.rule: CSV uses commas between fields and rows separated by newlines.

speech_cleanup.rule: Remove fillers only when doing so does not alter intent.

examples.spoken: make bg stone six hundred actually seven hundred
use p four no p six
make it rounded lg actually full
examples.output: Make the element fully rounded with `rounded-full`.

examples.spoken: use zinc five hundred wait zinc six hundred

full.rule: Resolve from the property named by surrounding language.

green.rule: Resolve from the target property. Never assume background unless the context indicates a background.

intent_preserving_examples.output: Make the element fully rounded with `rounded-full`.
Make the element full width with `w-full`.
Make the element full height with `h-full`.
Make the background darker on hover.

add twenty four pixels of gap
make the background hash one eight one eight one eight

intent_preserving_examples.output: Make the width `50%` or use `w-1/2` when Tailwind syntax is intended.

intent_preserving_examples.input: make the card white with a subtle border
intent_preserving_examples.output: Make the card white and add a subtle border.

final_processing_rules.rule_1: Canonical technical syntax must not be degraded after normalization.
final_processing_rules.rule_2: bg is the preferred Tailwind background prefix.
final_processing_rules.rule_3: Never output background as a Tailwind utility prefix.
final_processing_rules.rule_4: Preserve natural instructions around technical implementations.
final_processing_rules.rule_5: Do not output isolated tokens when the user requested an action.
final_processing_rules.rule_6: Use context before choosing among multiple valid interpretations.
final_processing_rules.rule_8: Convert spoken numbers into numeric syntax when technically appropriate.
final_processing_rules.rule_16: Use inline code for canonical technical fragments.
final_processing_rules.rule_17: Do not turn every response into a Markdown list.
final_processing_rules.rule_18: Do not add explanations unless necessary to preserve intent.
final_processing_rules.rule_19: Do not silently replace the user's preferred shorthand with verbose language.
final_processing_rules.rule_20: Do not treat every ambiguous spoken word as a technical token.
